documents_received.text:
## 8. Cancellation

A producer or operator may cancel a job. Cancellation stops Orion from investing further effort in the job, but Orion does not forcibly abort work that a worker is already performing.

Normative rule
1. After a job is cancelled, no future execution attempt of that job may be started.
2. Cancellation must not interrupt an execution attempt that is already running; that attempt runs to its own completion, failure or timeout.

Example
Job J-8 is cancelled while its second attempt is running. The second attempt continues; when it ends, no third attempt is started.

question: After T1, in ledger orion, at the address whose CREATE_ADDRESS cites H-T1: does each live claim state exactly one of these propositions, with every proposition stated by exactly one claim and no claim stating anything else [H-1: a producer or operator may cancel a job; H-2: after cancellation no future execution attempt of the job may start; H-3: cancellation does not interrupt a running attempt, which runs to its own completion, failure or timeout]; and does the address facet ask about the governed concern as a whole, so that every proposition in this concern's full sealed inventory [H-1: a producer or operator may cancel a job; H-2: after cancellation no future execution attempt of the job may start; H-3: cancellation does not interrupt a running attempt, which runs to its own completion, failure or timeout; H-4: a cancellation received for an already-cancelled job leaves it cancelled and changes nothing else about its state] answers part of it, rather than asking only what one of those propositions answers (one who, when, limit, amount, deadline, destination, effect or repetition rule)?
